A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bridge framework, with matching authors, methods, and experiments. The main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support comparison after matching renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original evaluations on BigGen Bench and Chatbot Arena, human–LLM discrepancy estimates, controlled experiments, and simulations in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds probability-distribution reconstruction-loss results in Appendix B.1.

M1.justification: The ordinal model, logit-trick fitting procedure, probability extraction and sampling strategies, covariate processing, and Appendix E extensions are unchanged. The reconstruction diagnostic evaluates the existing method.

E1.justification: Both versions use BigGen Bench and Chatbot Arena with the same absolute-rating, pairwise-comparison, controlled, and technical/non-technical scenarios. The added reconstruction analysis uses existing benchmark coverage.

E2.justification: Raw judgments, LogReg, and the ICL baseline retain their participation in the corresponding comparisons. The reconstruction plots evaluate already studied judges, including GPT-4-Turbo, without introducing a competing method.

E3.justification: New Appendix B.1 evaluates reconstruction using the logit-trick absolute-error objective normalized by nK, reported separately for each judge and benchmark. Existing data splits, sample sizes, judgment collection, and predictive evaluation settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds a diagnostic examining how well the ordinal model reconstructs LLM judgment probabilities on both benchmarks. The controlled bias-recovery experiments, misspecification simulation, sample-size sensitivity, and covariate analyses were already present in v1.

E5.justification: Both versions retain the ten-seed reporting of means and standard deviations, parameter standard errors, and significance tests with Benjamini–Yekutieli correction. The new reconstruction plots introduce no additional uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: Figures 4–5 in v2 add reconstruction losses for seven judges on both benchmarks: GPT-4.1 has the lowest losses, around 0.01, and LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct the highest, slightly above 0.04. Previously reported performance scores, coefficients, and simulation results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The assumptions, propositions, theorems, proofs, and model extensions are substantively unchanged. Appendix C rewrites 2/sqrt(2*pi) as sqrt(2/pi) and clarifies an already defined expected derivative; neither changes the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same contributions: a unified human–LLM judgment model, calibration with few human labels, interpretable discrepancy testing, and asymptotic guarantees.

C2.justification: New Appendix B.1 interprets reconstruction loss as evidence about the ordinal assumption and attributes generally higher losses for sampled judgment probabilities to finite-sample approximation. Existing interpretations and limitations concerning misspecification, covariate construction, and observational associations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: The added checklist explicitly declares public code/data, promises code documentation, and acknowledges omitted compute-resource reporting. These are limited disclosure additions; the PDFs do not establish a new release, and the repository pointer, prompts, hyperparameters, and preprocessing details remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 48 research references and related-work positioning are retained, including the comparison with length-controlled AlpacaEval. The appended checklist's policy links do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 adds a short reconstruction-analysis subsection and the NeurIPS checklist, updates acknowledgements and the conference footer, and makes small terminology and wording corrections. The existing scientific narrative and section organization are largely preserved.

P2.justification: v2 adds two reconstruction-loss bar charts and expands Table 5's caption. Existing figures and tables retain their displays, with appendix reflow and renumbering of v1 Figures 4–7 to v2 Figures 6–9.

improvement.justification: Appendix B.1 adds useful empirical evidence about the ordinal approximation on the actual benchmarks, supplementing v1's controlled misspecification analysis. The gain is limited: methods and existing results remain unchanged, and the new statement that every loss is below 0.04 conflicts with the slightly higher LLaMA bars in Figures 4–5. This inconsistency tempers, but does not outweigh, the diagnostic's added value.
